pr_body:
Fixes #12618, #12619, #12620, and #12621.

This PR fixes false positives for `Style/ArgumentsForwarding` when using block argument forwarding with other arguments.

And this PR makes `Style/ArgumentsForwarding` aware only block argument forwarding when using Ruby 3.1+.

-----------------

Before submitting the PR make sure the following are checked:

* [x] The PR relates to *only* one subject with a clear title and description in grammatically correct, complete sentences.
* [x] Wrote [good commit messages][1].
* [x] Commit message starts with `[Fix #issue-number]` (if the related issue exists).
* [x] Feature branch is up-to-date with `master` (if not - rebase it).
* [x] Squashed related commits together.
* [x] Added tests.
* [x] Ran `bundle exec rake default`. It executes all tests and runs RuboCop on its own code.
* [x] Added an entry (file) to the [changelog folder](https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/blob/master/changelog/) named `{change_type}_{change_description}.md` if the new code introduces user-observable changes. See [changelog entry format](https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#changelog-entry-format) for details.

[1]: https://chris.beams.io/posts/git-commit/

issue_context.title: False positive for Style/ArgumentsForwarding when only a block argument can be forwarded anonymously
issue_context.body:
In the new RuboCop version 1.60.0, the Style/ArgumentsForwarding cop now autocorrects argument lists with only a single block argument, or positional arguments combined with a block argument, to use `...` instead of the block argument. While this does not change things when the method is called in the original way, it does change the arity and will now forward (additional) positional and keyword arguments.

## Expected behavior

Given the following methods:
```ruby
def foo(&block)
  bar(&block)
end

def baz(qux, quuz, &block)
  bar(qux, quuz, &block)
end
```

I expect RuboCop _not_ to autocorrect when targeting Ruby before 3.1.

When targeting 3.1+, I expect it to autocorrect to:

```ruby
def foo(&)
  bar(&)
end

def baz(qux, quuz, &)
  bar(qux, quuz, &)
end
```

## Actual behavior

RuboCop autocorrects as follows, regardless of whether Ruby 3.0 or 3.1 is targeted.

```ruby
def foo(...)
  bar(...)
end

def baz(qux, quuz, ...)
  bar(qux, quuz, ...)
end
```

## Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Create a file `foo.rb` with the content given in the first code block above.
2. Run `rubocop -A`

## RuboCop version

```
$ bundle exec rubocop -V
1.60.0 (using Parser 3.3.0.3, rubocop-ast 1.30.0, running on ruby 3.3.0) [x86_64-linux]
  - rubocop-performance 1.20.2
  - rubocop-rspec 2.26.1
```

I think the changes that result in this behavior were introduced in #12541, where some RuboCop code was also (wrongly, I think) autocorrected.

@mvz I see what you're saying but I think it is actually the case prior to my change as well - certain autocorrects will change the arity of the method.

For example (this example converts `*args, &` to `...` which means kwargs are now accepted):

https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/blob/f0c62ef587e8cef80ddf5345648d15ad92768902/spec/rubocop/cop/style/arguments_forwarding_spec.rb#L759-L773

Similarly - converting just `**kwargs` to `...` means that positional args are now accepted:

https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/blob/f0c62ef587e8cef80ddf5345648d15ad92768902/spec/rubocop/cop/style/arguments_forwarding_spec.rb#L397-L411

Am I correct that these are the same issue?

> Am I correct that these are the same issue?

I think the first one is the same or else very similar. The second one is behind a non-default setting (`AllowOnlyRestArgument: false`), so that would be a conscious choice to allow a potential change in behavior.
